# Adjudication Task — Chapter 509

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃509화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|띠링.
  6|
  7|
  8|
  9|- 연계 퀘스트, [가짜 무림인 - 2단계]가 시작되었습니다!
 10|
 11|- 해당 퀘스트는 수락 여부에 관계 없이 강제 진행됩니다!
 12|
 13|- 퀘스트가 강제 수락되었습니다!
 14|
 15|
 16|
 17|“……?”
 18|
 19|뭐여, 시벌.
 20|
 21|생각이 표정으로 고스란히 드러난 모양이다. 나를 바라보던 문경의 눈썹이 꿈틀거렸다.
 22|
 23|“분명 다음 수련이 있다고 말했을 텐데, 설마 잊고 있었나?”
 24|
 25|“예?”
 26|
 27|아니, 잊긴 뭘 잊어. 지금 나랑 장난하나.
 28|
 29|어이가 없어진 나는 문경을 바라보며 되물었다.
 30|
 31|“그동안 제가 피똥을 몇 번을 쌌는데, 그걸 어떻게 잊습니까? 지금 생각해도 똥꼬가 움찔거립니다.”
 32|
 33|“……알겠으니 거기까지 해라. 더럽다.”
 34|
 35|“하, 진짜.”
 36|
 37|머리는 잊어도 똥꼬, 아니 몸은 기억하는 법.
 38|
 39|지금도 눈만 감으면 낮과 밤을 가리지 않고 피똥 싸던 기억이 새록새록 떠오른다.
 40|
 41|과장 좀 보태서, 지난 칠주야 동안 내가 쏟아 낸 핏물을 통에 담으면 호북성에 존재하는 모든 모기 새끼들이 모여 잔치를 벌일 수 있을 거다.
 42|
 43|‘끔찍했지.’
 44|
 45|그런 기억들은 잊으려고 해도 지워 지지가 않는다.
 46|
 47|문경과의 마지막 비무가 있던 날, 시스템 알림이 알려 주었던 연계 퀘스트도 마찬가지다.
 48|
 49|애초에 얼마 되지도 않은, 그리고 그만큼 중요한 일을 잊는다면 제정신이 아니지.
 50|
 51|“어쨌건 안 까먹고 똑똑히 기억하고 있습니다. 그때 하셨던 말씀 전부 다.”
 52|
 53|“그래?”
 54|
 55|문경이 나를 물끄러미 응시하며 물었다.
 56|
 57|“네놈의 말대로면 지금 보이는 반응이 더욱 이해가 안 되는군. 미리 알려 주기까지 했는데, 왜 뒤통수라도 한 대 맞은 표정이냐?”
 58|
 59|“……어.”
 60|
 61|진짜 뒤통수 맞은 기분이라 그렇지.
 62|
 63|다음 수련이 예정되어 있다는 건 알고 있었지만, 적어도 지금은 아닐 거라고 확신했다.
 64|
 65|일반적인 선박보다도 협소한 이 쾌조선에서 가르칠 수 있는 거라고 해 봐야 지극히 한정되어 있으니까.
 66|
 67|‘기껏해야 심법 정도?’
 68|
 69|하지만 무공과 공력의 근간이 되는 심법은 부품처럼 손쉽게 갈아 끼울 수 있는 것이 아니다.
 70|
 71|‘나 같은 경우에는 더더욱 그렇고.’
 72|
 73|열화신공은 그야말로 열화문의 뿌리다.
 74|
 75|공력의 성질을 화기(火氣)로 변화시키고, 그 힘을 증대화하는 것에 중점을 두어서 여타의 문파보다 심법이 차지하는 비중이 훨씬 높다고 할 수 있었다.
 76|
 77|다른 사람도 아니고 문경씩이나 되는 고수가 그 사실을 모를 리 없을 텐데…….
 78|
 79|나는 혹시나 하는 마음으로 물었다.
 80|
 81|“저기, 설마 심법 가르쳐 주시려고 하는 건 아니죠?”
 82|
 83|쉭, 촤악!
 84|
 85|바람 소리와 함께 고개를 틀자, 빛살처럼 쏘아진 비도(飛刀) 한 자루가 아슬아슬하게 목을 스쳐 지나가 등 뒤의 강물을 갈랐다.
 86|
 87|“……대답 잘 들었습니다.”
 88|
 89|“그따위 헛소리로 내 시간을 뺏지 마라.”
 90|
 91|“어휴, 그럼요. 저도 그냥 혹시나 해서 물어본 겁니다.”
 92|
 93|그럼 뭐지. 설마 또 독 시음회인가.
 94|
 95|불길함과 호기심이 동시에 엄습했지만, 지금 당장은 접어 두기로 했다.
 96|
 97|별다른 이유가 있어서가 아니라, 어느새 부쩍 멀어진 문경의 모습 때문이었다.
 98|
 99|촤아아아악.
100|
101|딱 좋은 바람과 뱃일에는 이골이 난 수적들의 존재도 영향이 있겠지만, 쾌조선이 나아가는 속도는 확실히 일반적인 선박보다 몇 수 위에 있었다.
102|
103|대화 몇 마디 나누지도 않았는데 벌써 저기까지 간 걸 보면 장강수로맹 놈들이 모터를 달아 놨는지 의심이 될 정도다.
104|
105|‘거, 더럽게 빠르네.’
106|
107|전교 1등을 밥 먹듯이 하는 우등생도 취약한 과목 하나쯤은 있기 마련이다. 내게는 경신법이 유독 그랬다.
108|
109|명색이 초절정 고수인만큼 등평도수(登萍渡水)의 수법으로 계속 따라가고는 있는데, 익숙하지 않을뿐더러 공력 소모도 상당했다.
110|
111|그렇다고 지난번 동정호에서처럼 밟고 다닐 만한 뭔가가 있는 것도 아니고.
112|
113|“우선 올라가서 듣겠습니다. 이 상태로 계속 있을 수는 없잖아요.”
114|
115|문경이 선선히 고개를 끄덕였다.
116|
117|“그렇게 해라.”
118|
119|“혹시 깜짝 선물로 암기 날리시는 건 아니죠?”
120|
121|“알겠으니 헛소리 그만하고 올라오기나 해라.”
122|
123|“옙.”
124|
125|나는 끌어올린 공력을 발끝에 집중시켰다.
126|
127|열화신공의 가장 큰 장점은 폭발적인 힘을 끌어낼 수 있다는 거다. 단 한 번의 도약이면 다시 쾌조선으로 들어가기에 차고 넘쳤다.
128|
129|하나, 둘.
130|
131|‘지금.’
132|
133|파앙!
134|
135|발끝에서 발출된 공력이 수면을 후려쳤다. 충격파로 강물이 거대한 벽처럼 솟구쳤고, 맹렬한 바람이 전신을 스쳤다.
136|
137|촌각이라고 할 수도 없을 만큼 짧은 순간에 십여 장의 거리를 지워 낸 나는 쾌조선의 선미(船尾)에 착륙…….
138|
139|빡!
140|
141|뭐여, 시벌.
142|
143|처음 거리를 좁혔을 때보다 더 빠른 속도로 튕겨 나간 나는, 황급히 공력을 발바닥으로 흘려보냄과 동시에 신형을 뒤집었다.
144|
145|수면을 향해 곤두박질치던 신형이 중심을 되찾으며 간신히 수면 위에 설 수 있었다.
146|
147|‘뭐지, 데자뷰인가.’
148|
149|나는 떨떠름한 눈빛으로 선미에 우뚝 선 문경을 바라보았다.
150|
151|“방금 뭡니까?”
152|
153|“뭐가 말이냐.”
154|
155|“손에 들고 계신 그거요. 그걸로 저 때리셨잖아요.”
156|
157|“아, 이거.”
158|
159|문경이 손에 들고 있던 커다란 무언가를 흔들었다.
160|
161|“이건 노라는 물건이다. 주로 배를 저을 때 쓰지.”
162|
163|“그걸 몰라서 여쭤본 게 아닌데요.”
164|
165|“그걸 몰라서 여쭤본 줄 알았다.”
166|
167|“이상한 짓 안 하기로 약속하지 않으셨습니까?”
168|
169|“정확히는 암기를 날리지 않겠다고 했지. 이건 암기가 아니다.”
170|
171|“아하, 그렇구나. 암기 대신 흉기를 사용하셨구나.”
172|
173|“그런 셈이지.”
174|
175|미친놈인가, 진짜.
176|
177|할 말을 잃어버린 나를 문경이 심유한 눈빛으로 응시했다. 아니, 정확히는 나를 중심으로 출렁이는 수면이다.
178|
179|“여전히 장강의 강물은 잔잔한데, 네놈의 발이 닿는 곳마다 난리통이로군.”
180|
181|“계속 이런 장난치시면 저 난리납니다, 진짜.”
182|
183|“왜 네놈만 유독 그러는지, 그 이유를 알고 있느냐?”
184|
185|“그건 모르겠고, 이러시는 이유가 뭡니까?”
186|
187|문경은 들은 척도 하지 않고 말을 이었다.
188|
189|“움직임이 투박하고 거칠기 때문이 아니다.”
190|
191|“성격 거칠어지게 만드시네.”
192|
193|“일정한 경지에 오른 고수의 움직임에는 저마다의 이유와 의미가 있다. 그리고 네놈의 경우에는 공력 자체가 폭급하기 때문이라고 할 수 있겠지. 이는 열화문의 무공이 가진 고질적인 문제점 중 하나다.”
194|
195|“아, 열 받네. 우선 다시 올라갈 테니까 손에 들고 계신 노부터 내려놓고…….”
196|
197|말을 이어 가던 나는 순간 멈칫했다.
198|
199|이게 단순한 심술이나 장난이 아니라는 사실을 깨달았기 때문이었다.
200|
201|“잠깐, 지금 뭐라고요?”
202|
203|“이제야 귓구멍이 뚫린 모양이로군. 물 위에서 네 움직임이 거친 이유가, 열화문의 무공이 가진 고질적인 문제라고 했다.”
204|
205|고질적인 문제라…….
206|
207|이건 가볍게 흘려들을 수 있는 이야기가 아니다.
208|
209|잠시 생각하던 나는 재차 입을 열었다.
210|
211|“그게 등평도수와 무슨 연관이 있습니까? 그냥 익숙하지 않아서 서툰 것뿐인데, 너무 쉽게 판단하시는 것 아니에요?”
212|
213|“멍청한 놈. 그리 단순한 문제가 아니다.”
214|
215|“그 말씀은…….”
216|
217|“공력의 안정성, 그리고 세밀함이지.”
218|
219|“안정성과 세밀함…….”
220|
221|“등평도수는 그 두 가지를 판단하는 척도 중 하나일 뿐이다. 공력의 움직임이 안정적이고 세밀한 자일수록 등평도수를 자유롭게 펼칠 수 있지. 비록 상승의 경신법이라고는 하나, 절정 고수 중에서도 조예가 깊은 자라면 그리 큰 어려움 없이 펼칠 수 있다.”
222|
223|막힘없이 말을 이어 간 문경이 돌연 선미에서 훌쩍 뛰어내렸다.
224|
225|평범한 사람이라면 얼굴 생김새조차 제대로 분간 못 할 만한 거리였지만, 극도로 예리한 감각의 소유자인 나는 똑똑히 보고, 들을 수 있었다.
226|
227|스윽.
228|
229|공기처럼 가볍게 수면에 착지한 문경의 모습을. 그리고 마치 아무 일도 없다는 듯, 잔물결 하나 일어나지 않는 수면을.
230|
231|문경의 건조한 눈빛이 나를 향했다.
232|
233|“반면 네놈은 어떠하냐?”
234|
235|“……!”
236|
237|나는 반사적으로 고개를 숙여 발아래를 내려다보았다. 그러나 결국 보나 마나 한 일이었다.
238|
239|내가 쾌조선을 쫓아 달려온 길은 또 다른 배가 지나간 것처럼 하얀 포말이 가득했으니까.
240|
241|촤악.
242|
243|신중하게 내디딘 걸음을 중심으로, 수십 개의 파문이 겹겹이 일어났다. 비교 대상이 문경이라 해도 너무 극심한 차이였다.
244|
245|“대답은 이미 스스로도 알고 있는 모양이군.”
246|
247|차라리 한심함과 비웃음이 담겨 있었다면 덜 부끄러웠을 거다.
248|
249|마치 ‘그래, 넌 그 정도지.’라고 말하는 듯한 문경의 고저 없는 목소리를 듣자 얼굴이 확 달아올랐다.
250|
251|“이제 내가 한 말의 뜻을 알겠느냐?”
252|
253|“……어느 정도는 알 것도 같습니다.”
254|
255|앞서 문경이 했던 말처럼 등평도수는 공력의 안정성과 세밀함을 볼 수 있는 중요한 척도였다.
256|
257|얼마나 힘을 잘 분배하고 제어하느냐에 따라 발걸음이 향하는 수면 위가 폭풍우라도 만난 것처럼 요동칠 수도, 인적 드문 호숫가처럼 잔잔할 수도 있다.
258|
259|“그럼 이를 통해 무엇을 얻어야 할지. 네놈의 입으로 직접 말해 봐라.”
260|
261|“음. 공력을 보다 효율적으로 다룰 수 있겠네요.”
262|
263|“답변이 마음에 들지 않는다.”
264|
265|“안정성과 세밀함은 물론이고, 같은 힘을 내면서도 공력의 소모를 줄일 수 있습니다.”
266|
267|“조금 나아졌군. 하지만 아직 부족하다.”
268|
269|1초가 1분처럼 느껴지는 시간 속, 곰곰이 생각에 잠겨 있던 나는 문득 입술을 뗐다.
270|
271|“증폭.”
272|
273|“더 자세히.”
274|
275|“앞서 말한 것들은 원하는 때에 적재적소의 힘을 발휘할 수 있는 조건이죠. 그리고 그만큼 공력을 세밀하게 조절할 수 있다면…… 지금보다 더욱 강하게 공력을 증폭시킬 수 있다는 뜻도 됩니다.”
276|
277|“그래서?”
278|
279|“단순히 안정성과 세밀함만을 추구하는 게 아니라, 제가 익힌 무공의 위력이 더욱 강력해진다. 맞습니까?”
280|
281|아무런 말 없이 나를 응시하던 문경이 한 마디를 툭 내뱉었다.
282|
283|“……아주 천치는 아니로군.”
284|
285|됐다. 정답이다.
286|
287|하지만 내가 묘한 희열을 느끼는 이유는, 사소하게나마 문경의 인정을 받았기 때문이 아니었다.
288|
289|‘만약 이번 수련을 성공적으로 해낸다면…… 지금보다 더 강해질 수 있다.’
290|

The Fire Gate Divine Technique was the very root of the Fire Gate Clan. It transformed the nature of our internal energy into fire qi and amplified its power, so the cultivation technique played a far greater role in our martial arts than it did in those of other sects.

[P32]
Mungyeong of all people had to know that, but I asked just in case.

[P33]
“Um, you’re not planning to teach me a cultivation technique, are you?”

[P34]
Whoosh! Slash!

[P35]
I turned my head at the sound of wind. A throwing blade shot past like a streak of light, grazing my neck before slicing through the river behind me.

[P36]
“……I heard your answer loud and clear.”

[P37]
“Don’t waste my time with that kind of nonsense.”

[P38]
“Of course. I was just asking on the off chance.”

[P39]
*Then what is it? Another poison-tasting session?*

[P40]
Foreboding and curiosity struck at once, but I put both aside for the moment. Not for any particular reason—Mungyeong had simply grown much farther away while we talked.

[P41]
Whoosh!

[P42]
The favorable wind and the waterway men’s sailing experience certainly helped, but the swift ship was several notches faster than an ordinary vessel.

[P43]
We’d barely exchanged a few words, yet he was already that far away. I almost wondered whether the bastards from the Yangtze River Channel League had installed a motor.

[P44]
*Damn, it’s fast.*

[P45]
Even a model student who routinely came first in the entire school was bound to have one weak subject. Mine was movement techniques.

[P46]
As befitted a Supreme Peak master, I could keep up using Rising on Duckweed, Crossing Water, but I wasn’t used to it, and it consumed a considerable amount of internal energy. Unlike on Dongting Lake last time, there was nothing here for me to step on, either.

[P47]
“I’ll climb aboard first and listen. I can’t stay out here like this.”

[P48]
Mungyeong nodded readily.

[P49]
“Do that.”

[P50]
“You’re not going to throw a hidden weapon at me as a surprise, are you?”

[P51]
“I said I understand. Stop talking nonsense and come up.”

[P52]
“Yes, sir.”

[P53]
I concentrated the internal energy I’d drawn up in my toes.

[P54]
The greatest advantage of the Fire Gate Divine Technique was the explosive force it could produce. One leap would be more than enough to get me back onto the swift ship.

[P55]
*One, two.*

[P56]
*Now.*

[P57]
Bang!

[P58]
Internal energy burst from my toes and slammed into the water. The shockwave sent the river surging upward like a massive wall, and a fierce wind swept over me.

[P59]
In less than a moment, I covered more than ten *jang* and landed on the swift ship’s stern—

[P60]
Thwack!

[P61]
*What the fuck?*

[P62]
I went flying back even faster than I’d approached. I hurriedly sent internal energy into the soles of my feet and flipped myself around.

[P63]
I’d been plunging headfirst toward the river, but I regained my balance just in time to stand on its surface.

[P64]
*What is this, déjà vu?*

[P65]
I looked sourly at Mungyeong, who stood on the stern.

[P66]
“What was that?”

[P67]
“What was what?”

[P68]
“That thing in your hand. You hit me with it.”

[P69]
“Oh, this.”

[P70]
Mungyeong waved the large object he was holding.

[P71]
“This is an oar. It’s mainly used to row a boat.”

[P72]
“I wasn’t asking because I didn’t know that.”

[P73]
“I thought you were.”

[P74]
“Didn’t you promise not to do anything strange?”

[P75]
“To be precise, I said I wouldn’t throw a hidden weapon. This isn’t a hidden weapon.”

[P76]
“Oh, I see. You used a lethal weapon instead.”

[P77]
“Something like that.”

[P78]
*Is he insane? Seriously.*

[P79]
Mungyeong gave me a searching look. No—he was looking at the water rippling around me.

[P80]
“The Yangtze is still calm, yet wherever your feet touch, the water erupts.”

[P81]
“If you keep pulling stunts like this, *I’m* going to erupt. Seriously.”

[P82]
“Do you know why it happens to you in particular?”

[P83]
“I don’t, but why are you doing this?”

[P84]
Mungyeong ignored my question.

[P85]
“It isn’t because your movements are clumsy and rough.”

[P86]
“You’re going to make *me* rough.”

[P87]
“Every movement a master of a certain realm makes has its own reason and purpose. In your case, the cause is your internal energy itself. It’s too violent. This is one of the longstanding problems with the Fire Gate Clan’s martial arts.”

[P88]
“Ah, now I’m pissed. I’ll climb aboard again, so put down that oar first and—”

[P89]
I stopped mid-sentence.

[P90]
This wasn’t just Mungyeong being spiteful or playing a prank.

[P91]
“Wait. What did you just say?”

[P92]
“So your ears do work. I said the reason your movements are rough on the water is a longstanding problem with the Fire Gate Clan’s martial arts.”

[P93]
*A longstanding problem…*

[P94]
I couldn’t brush that off.

[P95]
After a moment’s thought, I asked, “What does that have to do with Rising on Duckweed, Crossing Water? I’m just clumsy because I’m not used to it. Aren’t you judging too quickly?”

[P96]
“You fool. It isn’t that simple.”

[P97]
“You mean…”

[P98]
“The stability and precision of your internal energy.”

[P99]
“Stability and precision…”

[P100]
“Rising on Duckweed, Crossing Water is one measure of those qualities. The more stable and precise your internal energy, the more freely you can perform it. It’s an advanced movement technique, but a Peak master with deep enough attainment can use it without much difficulty.”

[P101]
Mungyeong finished speaking and suddenly leaped down from the stern.

[P102]
He was far enough away that an ordinary person wouldn’t have been able to make out his face. But my senses were keen enough to see and hear him clearly.

[P103]
Softly, he landed on the water, as light as air. Not a ripple rose around him. It was as though nothing had happened.

[P104]
Mungyeong turned his dry gaze on me.

[P105]
“And you?”

[P106]
“……!”

[P107]
I lowered my head to look beneath my feet, though I already knew what I’d find.

[P108]
The path I’d taken chasing the swift ship was covered in white foam, as though another boat had passed through it.

[P109]
Splash.

[P110]
I took a cautious step. Dozens of ripples spread out from it, overlapping one another.

[P111]
Even compared with Mungyeong, the difference was too great.

[P112]
“You seem to know the answer yourself.”

[P113]
I might have felt less embarrassed if he’d sounded scornful. Instead, his flat voice seemed to say, *Yes, that’s about your level.* My face burned.

[P114]
“Do you understand what I meant now?”

[P115]
“……I think I’m starting to.”

[P116]
As Mungyeong had said, Rising on Duckweed, Crossing Water was an important measure of the stability and precision of one’s internal energy.

[P117]
Depending on how well you distributed and controlled your power, the water beneath your feet could churn as though caught in a storm or remain as calm as a deserted lakeshore.

[P118]
“Then tell me what you should gain from this. In your own words.”

[P119]
“Hmm. I’ll be able to use my internal energy more efficiently.”

[P120]
“I don’t like that answer.”

[P121]
“I’ll gain stability and precision, and I’ll be able to produce the same amount of force while using less internal energy.”

[P122]
“A little better. Still not enough.”

[P123]
Each second seemed to stretch into a minute as I thought it over. Then the answer came to me.

[P124]
“Amplification.”

[P125]
“Explain.”

[P126]
“What I’ve said so far would let me apply the right amount of force where and when I need it. If I can control my internal energy that precisely… I can amplify it more than I do now, too.”

[P127]
“So?”

[P128]
“This isn’t just about stability and precision. The martial arts I’ve learned will become more powerful. Am I right?”

[P129]
Mungyeong stared at me for a moment, then tossed out a single remark.

[P130]
“……You’re not a complete idiot.”

[P131]
*That’s it. I got it right.*

[P132]
But the strange thrill I felt wasn’t from winning a little praise from Mungyeong.

[P133]
*If I can complete this training, I can become stronger than I am now.*

[P134]
I’d hit a kind of stagnation. Maybe I’d grown too quickly. After advancing by leaps and bounds, my martial arts had stopped progressing, and I could feel a high wall blocking my path.

[P135]
But with this training, I could improve my technique even without gaining some new enlightenment.

[P136]
*So I still had plenty of room to grow without enlightenment.*

[P137]
When had I started thinking about it all wrong? I hadn’t tried to fill the space I already had. I’d just kept wanting something newer and greater.

[P138]
*What a stupid thing to do.*

[P139]
It was like owning a one-terabyte external hard drive, filling only five hundred gigabytes of it with porn, then whining that I was out of space.

[P140]
Mungyeong had shown me that I still had another five hundred gigabytes for porn—no, that I still had room to fill. No need to buy another external hard drive when the first one wasn’t full.

[P141]
*Ah, Great Lord Mun.*

[P142]
A halo seemed to shine behind Mungyeong’s shoulder.

[P143]
He caught the look in my eyes and spoke.

[P144]
“Keep your eyes straight ahead before I gouge them out.”

[P145]
“……Ah, yes.”

[P146]
“Anyway, you seem to have finally grasped the general idea.”

[P147]
“Yes. I think I get it.”

[P148]
“Then you must know what training you need to do now.”

[P149]
Of course I did. I gave the answer I’d been expecting.

[P150]
“Rising on Duckweed, Crossing Water. Am I right?”

[P151]
“Yes. Better to experience it yourself than hear and think about it a hundred times. The Yangtze is the perfect place, so start now.”

[P152]
So that was why he’d knocked me into the water without warning. He must have planned this from the beginning.

[P153]
But I wasn’t annoyed or resentful. You couldn’t gain anything without paying a price.

[P154]
*It’s a little daunting with nothing but river around me, but I’ll get used to it if I keep practicing.*

[P155]
I answered without hesitation.

[P156]
“Understood.”

[P157]
“You’re more obedient than I expected. Keep that attitude.”

[P158]
“Yes.”

[P159]
If it meant getting stronger, what wouldn’t I do?

[P160]
I bowed to Mungyeong. Then I realized I’d forgotten the most important question.

[P161]
“Um, by the way.”

[P162]
“Hmm?”

[P163]
“How long do I have to do this?”

[P164]
“What a foolish question.”

[P165]
Mungyeong spread both hands as though the answer were obvious.

[P166]
*Ten stars… no, ten shichen?*

[P167]
“W-wait. Even for me, ten shichen is impossible. I have to keep up with the swift ship using Rising on Duckweed, Crossing Water. You know how much internal energy that’ll take—”

[P168]
“What are you talking about? Ten days.”

[P169]
“Excuse me?”

[P170]
“Not ten shichen. Ten days. Follow us all the way to Henan.”

[P171]
“……Excuse me?”

[P172]
As I froze in place, a familiar notification rang in my ears.

[P173]
Ding.

[P174]
> **System**
>
> - The training method for **Fake Murim Martial Artist—Stage 2** has been newly established!
> - The Instructor has set the training period to **10 days**! This period may become shorter or longer depending on when you reach the destination!
> - The countdown begins now! Hang in there—argh!
> - **Time limit:** 9 days 23 hours 59 minutes 59 seconds.

[P175]
“……”

[P176]
*Fuck. I have no words.*

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.

- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.

- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

“Ah, now I’m pissed. I’ll climb aboard again, so put down that oar first and—”

[P89]
I stopped mid-sentence.

[P90]
This wasn’t just Mungyeong being spiteful or playing a prank.

[P91]
“Wait. What did you just say?”

[P92]
“So your ears do work. I said the reason your movements are rough on the water is a longstanding problem with the Fire Gate Clan’s martial arts.”

[P93]
*A longstanding problem…*

[P94]
I couldn’t brush that off.

[P95]
After a moment’s thought, I asked, “What does that have to do with Rising on Duckweed, Crossing Water? I’m just clumsy because I’m not used to it. Aren’t you judging too quickly?”

[P96]
“You fool. It isn’t that simple.”

[P97]
“You mean…”

[P98]
“The stability and precision of your internal energy.”

[P99]
“Stability and precision…”

[P100]
“Rising on Duckweed, Crossing Water is one measure of those qualities. The more stable and precise your internal energy, the more freely you can perform it. It’s an advanced movement technique, but a Peak master with deep enough attainment can use it without much difficulty.”

[P101]
Mungyeong finished speaking and suddenly leaped down from the stern.

[P102]
He was far enough away that an ordinary person wouldn’t have been able to make out his face. But my senses were keen enough to see and hear him clearly.

[P103]
Softly, he landed on the water, as light as air. Not a ripple rose around him. It was as though nothing had happened.

[P104]
Mungyeong turned his dry gaze on me.

[P105]
“And you?”

[P106]
“……!”

[P107]
I lowered my head to look beneath my feet, though I already knew what I’d find.

[P108]
The path I’d taken chasing the swift ship was covered in white foam, as though another boat had passed through it.

[P109]
Splash.

[P110]
I took a cautious step. Dozens of ripples spread out from it, overlapping one another.

[P111]
Even compared with Mungyeong, the difference was too great.

[P112]
“You seem to know the answer yourself.”

[P113]
I might have felt less embarrassed if he’d sounded scornful. Instead, his flat voice seemed to say, *Yes, that’s about your level.* My face burned.

[P114]
“Do you understand what I meant now?”

[P115]
“……I think I’m starting to.”

[P116]
As Mungyeong had said, Rising on Duckweed, Crossing Water was an important measure of the stability and precision of one’s internal energy.

[P117]
Depending on how well you distributed and controlled your power, the water beneath your feet could churn as though caught in a storm or remain as calm as a deserted lakeshore.

[P118]
“Then tell me what you should gain from this. In your own words.”

[P119]
“Hmm. I’ll be able to use my internal energy more efficiently.”

[P120]
“I don’t like that answer.”

[P121]
“I’ll gain stability and precision, and I’ll be able to produce the same amount of force while using less internal energy.”

[P122]
“A little better. Still not enough.”

[P123]
Each second seemed to stretch into a minute as I thought it over. Then the answer came to me.

[P124]
“Amplification.”

[P125]
“Explain.”

[P126]
“What I’ve said so far would let me apply the right amount of force where and when I need it. If I can control my internal energy that precisely… I can amplify it more than I do now, too.”

[P127]
“So?”

[P128]
“This isn’t just about stability and precision. The martial arts I’ve learned will become more powerful. Am I right?”

[P129]
Mungyeong stared at me for a moment, then tossed out a single remark.

[P130]
“……You’re not a complete idiot.”

[P131]
*That’s it. I got it right.*

[P132]
But the strange thrill I felt wasn’t from winning a little praise from Mungyeong.

[P133]
*If I can complete this training, I can become stronger than I am now.*

[P134]
I’d hit a kind of stagnation. Maybe I’d grown too quickly. After advancing by leaps and bounds, my martial arts had stopped progressing, and I could feel a high wall blocking my path.

[P135]
But with this training, I could improve my technique even without gaining some new enlightenment.

[P136]
*So I still had plenty of room to grow without enlightenment.*

[P137]
When had I started thinking about it all wrong? I hadn’t tried to fill the space I already had. I’d just kept wanting something newer and greater.

[P138]
*What a stupid thing to do.*

[P139]
It was like owning a one-terabyte external hard drive, filling only five hundred gigabytes of it with porn, then whining that I was out of space.

[P140]
Mungyeong had shown me that I still had another five hundred gigabytes for porn—no, that I still had room to fill. No need to buy another external hard drive when the first one wasn’t full.

[P141]
*Ah, Great Lord Mun.*

[P142]
A halo seemed to shine behind Mungyeong’s shoulder.

[P143]
He caught the look in my eyes and spoke.

[P144]
“Keep your eyes straight ahead before I gouge them out.”

[P145]
“……Ah, yes.”

[P146]
“Anyway, you seem to have finally grasped the general idea.”

[P147]
“Yes. I think I get it.”

[P148]
“Then you must know what training you need to do now.”

[P149]
Of course I did. I gave the answer I’d been expecting.

[P150]
“Rising on Duckweed, Crossing Water. Am I right?”

[P151]
“Yes. Better to experience it yourself than hear and think about it a hundred times. The Yangtze is the perfect place, so start now.”

[P152]
So that was why he’d knocked me into the water without warning. He must have planned this from the beginning.

[P153]
But I wasn’t annoyed or resentful. You couldn’t gain anything without paying a price.

[P154]
*It’s a little daunting with nothing but river around me, but I’ll get used to it if I keep practicing.*

[P155]
I answered without hesitation.

[P156]
“Understood.”

[P157]
“You’re more obedient than I expected. Keep that attitude.”

[P158]
“Yes.”

[P159]
If it meant getting stronger, what wouldn’t I do?

[P160]
I bowed to Mungyeong. Then I realized I’d forgotten the most important question.

[P161]
“Um, by the way.”

[P162]
“Hmm?”

[P163]
“How long do I have to do this?”

[P164]
“What a foolish question.”

[P165]
Mungyeong spread both hands as though the answer were obvious.

[P166]
*Ten stars… no, ten shichen?*

[P167]
“W-wait. Even for me, ten shichen is impossible. I have to keep up with the swift ship using Rising on Duckweed, Crossing Water. You know how much internal energy that’ll take—”

[P168]
“What are you talking about? Ten days.”

[P169]
“Excuse me?”

[P170]
“Not ten shichen. Ten days. Follow us all the way to Henan.”

[P171]
“……Excuse me?”

[P172]
As I froze in place, a familiar notification rang in my ears.

[P173]
Ding.

[P174]
> **System**
>
> - The training method for **Fake Murim Martial Artist—Stage 2** has been newly established!
> - The Instructor has set the training period to **10 days**! This period may become shorter or longer depending on when you reach the destination!
> - The countdown begins now! Hang in there—argh!
> - **Time limit:** 9 days 23 hours 59 minutes 59 seconds.

[P175]
“……”

[P176]
*Fuck. I have no words.*

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.
